global_organization_chain: A compact decision preview covering NetLogo, more than 700 combinations, symmetric fanning, electronic lanes, and autonomous cars.
A symmetric merge, preserved driver patience, and a user-facing model are offered as preliminary guidance.
A bounded research problem linking lane geometry, payment method, traffic, and vehicle type.
A typed list of lane, booth, payment, vehicle, traffic, and satisfaction inputs.
A conditional scope for the simulation: symmetric entry, fixed payment lanes, stochastic human behavior, and patient autonomous cars.
A configurable NetLogo world with variable lane count, booth count, traffic, payment, and vehicle type.
A procedural execution chain for creating cars, operating booths, moving forward, choosing lanes, and removing exits.
A car state vector containing driver, speed, top-speed, target-lane, patience, payment method, service time, and anticipation.
A discrete road world with colored patches, barriers, spawn points, toll gates, and an exit condition.
A motion rule set plus a 0.5 patch/tick, 18 feet/patch, approximately 10 ticks/second calibration.
Equation (1) combines standardized cost, wait, safety, and throughput terms and is minimized.
Symmetric fanning has the best reported satisfaction for 3/4, 4/6, and 6/9 configurations.
A reporter stream for merges, completed cars, average patience, and below-threshold speed.
Lower patience produces more merges; the effect tapers after a threshold and is reproduced in the 6/9 layout.
The 0%-25% autonomous sweep is nearly flat; accumulated efficiency declines as starting cars increase.
A flexible, visual, user-friendly model whose reported results remain limited by runtime and exploration constraints.
Symmetric merges and preserved driver patience are the paper's principal recommendations.
Future work includes signal-staggered booth release and explicit human/exact-change comparisons.
Thirteen references identify the external context and tools but do not supply the missing run ledger.

moves: input: [ABS Summary] A toll plaza must trade congestion, safety, payment technology, and construction choices.
rhetorical job: [ABS Summary] Preview the agent model, scenario sweep, symmetric design finding, and authority-facing use in the order the paper executes them.
analytical job: [ABS Summary] Keep the headline claims attached to their simulation variables and comparison boundaries.
output: [ABS Summary] A compact decision preview covering NetLogo, more than 700 combinations, symmetric fanning, electronic lanes, and autonomous cars.
handoff: [ABS Summary] The letter and introduction unpack the public-road mechanism and the later model chain.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put warnings last.

moves: input: [MEM Authority letter] The New Jersey Turnpike needs a safer and more efficient toll-plaza configuration.
rhetorical job: [MEM Authority letter] Address the authority directly, restate the mechanism, and turn preliminary findings into conditional practical advice.
analytical job: [MEM Authority letter] Separate the letter's claimed result, the model's evidence, and the explicit invitation to continue testing.
output: [MEM Authority letter] A symmetric merge, preserved driver patience, and a user-facing model are offered as preliminary guidance.
handoff: [MEM Authority letter] The introduction formalizes the problem and names the variables that the letter leaves qualitative.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put warnings last.

moves: input: [INT 1 Introduction] Toll plazas fan many service lanes back into fewer highway lanes and can create queues and unsafe merges.
rhetorical job: [INT 1 Introduction] Move from national context to the New Jersey mechanism, then motivate automation and a design comparison.
analytical job: [INT 1 Introduction] Distinguish public motivation, local bottleneck, payment-technology question, and the paper's proposed contribution.
output: [INT 1 Introduction] A bounded research problem linking lane geometry, payment method, traffic, and vehicle type.
handoff: [INT 1 Introduction] The problem analysis turns that motivation into explicit design criteria.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put warnings last.

moves: input: [ANL 2 Analysis of the Problem] The prompt asks for a best plaza design across lanes, booths, merge shapes, flow, safety, and cost.
rhetorical job: [ANL 2 Analysis of the Problem] Restate the prompt as a sequence of measurable design tasks before selecting NetLogo.
analytical job: [ANL 2 Analysis of the Problem] Map each requested criterion to a later metric and preserve the distinction between design variables and operating conditions.
output: [ANL 2 Analysis of the Problem] A typed list of lane, booth, payment, vehicle, traffic, and satisfaction inputs.
handoff: [ANL 2 Analysis of the Problem] The assumptions make the typed problem tractable.

analytical job: [ASM 3 Assumptions and Justification] Keep payment, behavior, geometry, and cost assumptions separate so each can be challenged independently.
output: [ASM 3 Assumptions and Justification] A conditional scope for the simulation: symmetric entry, fixed payment lanes, stochastic human behavior, and patient autonomous cars.

analytical job: [DEV 4.1 Model Development] Connect micro-level car attributes to macro-level throughput, queueing, and merge outcomes.

main_argument_chains.claim: A symmetric merge is preferred in the tested lane/booth layouts.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat symmetry as a tested candidate and rerun it with replicated, calibrated conflict measures.

main_argument_chains.claim: Patience changes merge activity and can alter system efficiency.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Test behavioral interventions separately from geometry and preserve the finite-run boundary.

main_argument_chains.claim: The reported autonomous effect is negligible in the tested range.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not extrapolate beyond 25 percent or confuse autonomous type with EZ-Pass payment.

main_argument_chains.claim: The model is useful as an inspectable scenario tool but not yet a validated field design.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Archive code and replications before construction or public operational decisions.

warnings.warning: The exponential service-rate notation is not accompanied by a fitted distribution or random-seed ledger.

The printed conversion multiplies by seconds/(95 feet) but reports tick/second; preserve the source expression and flag the dimensional-direction and numerical-convention ambiguity instead of silently repairing it.
The satisfaction score uses a safety term whose direction should be checked against the merge-count proxy.
The throughput aggregation lacks repeated-run uncertainty and can change with the traffic-level denominator.
The accumulated-efficiency equation does not by itself establish a general efficiency law across populations.
